description:
A plugin that expands and improves the plugin experience

Requirements:
exteraGram: 12.9.0 and above
AyuGram: 12.10.6 and above
easter_egg_info: 100GB of Epstein files is for the weak, the strong have 14GB of KPM files
faq_1_a:
KPM (Kangel Plugins Manager) is a plugin for easy plugin management. Already available: updating **all** plugins with one button, automatic library fetching (if a plugin needs, say, CactusLib, CactusLib is installed first and only then the plugin itself), and deeplink support for quick installation.

Example for Steam: [tg://kpm_install?plugin=steam](tg://kpm_install?plugin=steam)
faq_2_a:
A category is what the plugin does: it shows information — Information; other plugins depend on it — Library. There are six categories: Customization, Utilities, Information, Messages, Entertainment, Library.

The filter is enabled by tapping **Install plugins** in the installation menu.
faq_3_a:
To export, go to **Settings → KPM → Plugin management → Export collection**, select plugins and create a collection.

To import, go to **Settings → KPM → Plugin management → Import collection** and pick a .kpm file — or just tap such a file in a chat.
faq_3_q: How do I export or import plugins?
faq_4_a: The plugin link is available via the button in the plugin menu.
faq_4_q: How do I get a hyperlink (tg://...)?
faq_5_a: Send your plugin for review to the admins via the @KPMAppealBot bot.
faq_5_q: How do I submit my plugin to the store?
faq_6_a: KPM repositories also include every plugin from @exteraPluginsSup, so this is normal — nobody made a mistake.
faq_6_q: Why do KPM repositories contain my plugins that I never published there?
faq_7_a: Refresh the plugin list by tapping [here](tg://kpm_list) or simply pull down the store list.
faq_7_q: New plugins do not show up in the store, what should I do?
guide_ai_text:
**AI search** finds plugins from a plain description: just say what you need.

Pick a provider and a model here and paste the API key. The search button itself lives in the plugin list.
guide_offer_text: A minute or two: where everything lives and what is worth your attention.
guide_s1_text:
KPM installs, updates and manages plugins for you.

Everything lives in one place — the settings screen open behind this card. Seven sections, and this guide walks through them.
guide_s2_text:
**Plugin management** — install from the store, a file or a link, update everything at once, clear the cache.

**Collections**: export your plugin set and restore it on another device.
guide_s3_text:
**Auto updates** — refresh the store on start and update installed plugins on their own.

An update you do not want can be ignored: it stops asking until you take it off the ignored list.
guide_s4_text:
**An unverified plugin is code inside your account:** it can read your chats and act on your behalf.

**Blocking such plugins is on by default — leave it on.** KPM scans files, dangerous calls and network use before install, and anything shady can be sent to the check bot from this section.
guide_s5_text:
**Interface** — buttons on the plugins screen, the pill in search, inline search in any chat, bubbles with plugin status and smart search.

Anything you do not need can be turned off here.
guide_s6_text:
**Help & Guide** — replay the onboarding tour and open the FAQ with answers to common questions.

**Debugging** holds logs and device info, and **About** has the forum, source code and devs.
guide_s7_text:
Questions are answered in the FAQ — the button below opens it.

The guide can be opened again at any time: settings, section **Other**.

t_acckill: Account sign-out/deletion in code (check the logic)
t_bot_token: Possible hardcoded bot token ({n}) + data sending
t_c2: Looks like a control channel: socket with send and receive
t_c2_chain: C2 chain on one socket: connect → send → recv
t_cloud: Data sent to cloud upload (possible exfiltration)
t_daemon: Background thread with infinite loop (usually harmless)
t_datathief: Suspicious keywords in text (often a false positive)
t_destructive: Destructive file operations (removal of system/client files)
t_dex: DEX code loading over network (possible dropper)
t_embedded_b64: Discovered and decompiled hidden Base64 payload ({name})
t_exec_net: Possible remote code execution: exec() + network
t_exec_net_chain: Network code execution (chain: net data → exec)
t_filename: Suspicious file name (often a false positive)
t_harvest: Member/history reading + sending outside (possible data collection)
t_killproc: Process termination (usually a restart, please verify)
t_session: Session file reading + sending outside (possible session theft)
t_spam: Message sending from background thread (possible spam)
t_tg_intercept: Hidden interception of outgoing messages and media
